subject: Private hosting: connectivity implications & procurement checkpoint
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@quantix.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting: connectivity implications & procurement checkpoint

Alex — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a clear set of next actions. Please reply with anything I missed.

Summary of the customer's stated drivers
- Regulatory/data residency: clinical trial data for EU/US sites; primary requirement is that PHI stays in customer-controlled VPC and logs retained per their retention policy.
- Air-gap/isolated hosting: preference for private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with limited egress; procurement team flagged air-gap as a potential must for one of their trials.
- Network constraints: Quantix currently blocks outbound internet from compute. Any integration will need either (a) a managed egress proxy that is allowlisted, or (b) VPC peering/privatelink to Redwood endpoints.
- Performance: low-latency inference required for batch inference (<=200ms p90) for the clinician UI; expectation of predictable throughput for pilot (up to 5 qps sustained).

What we committed today
- Redwood will produce a short connectivity checklist tailored to an air-gapped/allowlist environment (attachment: redwood_private_checklist_v1.xlsx).
- We'll surface recommended network patterns: VPC peering + private endpoints, or an on-prem appliance pattern if they cannot open any outbound egress.
- Provide our SOC2/HIPAA artifacts and a secure intake path for Quantix to request additional evidence.
- Introduce procurement PO flow and sample SOW template for Dedicated/private hosting pricing.

Open questions / clarifications needed from your side
- Can you confirm whether the blocking of outbound internet applies to management-plane traffic (i.e., Will hosts be allowed to talk to a private endpoint hosted in AWS us-west-2?)
- Who on Procurement should we loop in for contract/CDs? You mentioned procurement@quantix.health — please confirm the contact name and preferred procurement cadence (SOW, PO, or master services agreement).
- Expected pilot start: you mentioned "late July" tentatively. Can you confirm target dates and whether we should plan for a 6-week technical ramp?

Next steps (action owners)
- Stephanie (Redwood): Share checklist, example private endpoint config, and a short packet on SLAs and pricing ranges for Dedicated/private by Thu 6/24. (Attachment attached).
- Marissa (Redwood Solutions): Offer to attend an infra deep-dive if Quantix wants to validate firewall rules and VPC flows.
- Alex (Quantix): Send procurement contact + any internal security questionnaire (if you have a prioritized list, attach to reply).

Attachments referenced: redwood_private_checklist_v1.xlsx

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

> Thanks Stephanie — the call was helpful. I’ll post the two items you asked for: the security questionnaire and the procurement contact.

> A couple items to call out straight away: our network team will only allow outbound to a handful of pre-approved endpoints and only over TLS. From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@quantix.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@quantix.health>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting: connectivity implications & procurement checkpoint

Stephanie — thanks for the summary and checklist. A few clarifications to keep everyone moving: 

1) Network posture
- Confirmed: outbound is heavily restricted. Our security team will only allow TLS 443 egress to an allowlist. No arbitrary outbound to the internet.
- Preferred approach: either a private endpoint (managed by Redwood) reachable over peered VPC/privatelink, or an on-prem gateway. We can do VPC peering in AWS if you publish an endpoint IP range; otherwise privatelink is our preferred path.

2) Procurement and timeline
- Procurement contact: Priya Menon (procurement@quantix.health) — she’s looped in on this reply. Their cadence is typically PO + SOW for pilots. For larger programs we use an MSA.
- Timeline: target pilot kickoff week of July 26. We need an internal security review completed by July 10 to meet that.

3) Security artifacts
- Attaching our security requirements doc for context (Quantix-Security-Requirements.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can provide: SOC2 report (recent), network penetration testing summary, and a contact for KMS/HSM integration questions.

4) Performance ask
- For the pilot we do not need multi-region; single-region (us-west-2) is fine. But we want a clear latency baseline and a runbook for degraded modes (e.g., fallback to a smaller model).

Let us know if you want to schedule the infra deep-dive next week — our infra engineer (Kyle) can join.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Principal Infrastructure Architect, Quantix Health
alex.johnson@quantix.health

Attachments: Quantix-Security-Requirements.pdf

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Alex — copying Priya for procurement items. Quick follow-up and concrete next steps so we all have aligned owners and dates:

Deliverables from Redwood (w/ tentative dates)
- Finalized connectivity checklist (redwood_private_checklist_v1.xlsx) — by Thu 6/24 (Stephanie)
- Private endpoint configuration options (peering / privatelink diagram + IP ranges) — by Mon 6/28 (Marissa + Solutions Architecture)
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 summary, penetration test summary) — shared via secure drive link by Mon 6/28 (Security team). Link: https://drive.google.com/qx/secure-artifacts/quantix-reqs
- Pricing ballpark for a 3-month pilot (Dedicated capacity) — by Wed 6/30 (Sales pricing)

Proposed next meetings
- Infra deep-dive (technical) — Tue 6/29 at 10:00 PT (Marissa + Redwood infra + Quantix Kyle). Please confirm.
- Procurement sync (contract path and expected SOW) — week of 7/6 (Stephanie + Priya).

Procurement note to Priya: we’ll prepare a sample SOW and a short commercial summary for pilot PO. If you have an internal PO template or specific insurance language, please share so we can validate early.

Action items for Quantix
- Priya / procurement: confirm PO vs MSA preference for pilot and share any mandatory contract clauses (insurance, data handling).
- Alex / infra: confirm whether privatelink is acceptable or if you require public IP ranges for peering.

I’ll follow up with calendar invites and the checklist file (attached). If the timeline shifts, call out the blocker and we’ll reprioritize.

Thanks — looking forward to the infra session.
